steps.title: Nominalization and impersonal phrasing: sound concise without hiding the claim
steps.body: Formal reports often turn actions into nouns (les coûts augmentent → une hausse des coûts). Nominalization can make a comparison concise, but too many abstract nouns can hide who did what. Use an impersonal phrase (il semble que, il est possible que) to mark a cautious interpretation, not to avoid naming a source. Keep the actor or evidence visible when it matters: les ménages interrogés signalent… Before using a noun phrase, ask whether a clear verb would be easier to understand.

steps.title: Nominalization and impersonal phrasing: sound concise without hiding the claim
rows: Les frais ont augmenté pendant la période.
Une hausse des frais a été observée.
An increase in costs was observed.
Il semble que les coûts soient plus élevés.
It appears that costs are higher.
Selon les ménages interrogés, le transport coûte davantage.
According to the households surveyed, transportation costs more.
Les chiffres ne permettent pas de prévoir chaque dépense.
The figures do not allow every expense to be predicted.

steps.prompt: Which version makes the actor clear?
options: Il y a une hausse, car demain.
Une hausse fut opérée par le signalement.
Les ménages interrogés signalent une hausse.
La hausse est une moyenne de contrat.
steps.explain: The direct sentence names who reported the increase.

steps.prompt: What does il semble que do?
steps.explain: It presents an interpretation cautiously; evidence still matters.

options: They can hide who did what
They cannot be used in writing
They always change a noun's gender
steps.explain: A dense series of abstract nouns can obscure the actor and action.
